payload.blocks: Conflict C6 of the rule gathering: the routing skill. Its other rows land; the plan is not done until this is answered.
payload.headline: Do work items still route by stage, or only by their workflow run?

parts.cause: The workflow spec keeps 'Work has no stage', but the state code still derives `workflowStep` from a legacy `stage`, so older items still carry one. The skill is half in each model.

options.cost: About 15 lines in one skill, no code.
options.does: An item with a workflow run id is driven through its run; an item without one is routed by its `workflowStep`, called the legacy-item route.
options.gain: Describes what the code does today and is true of spec and code.
options.label: A. Both, named

options.cost: About 60 lines and a new item.
options.does: Rewrite the skill to the run model and drop the stage table.
options.harm: Older items get no instructions; a decision on them and an item for the legacy path are needed.
options.label: B. Run only

options.does: Revert the paragraph that says work has no stage.
options.label: C. Stage only

parts.recommendation: A: it is true of both spec and code and loses no rule.

scope.allows: Editing the routing skill lines about stage and `workflowStep` only, as in option A.
scope.forbids: Removing the stage field from the state code, changing the spec, or touching other skills.

parts.what: The routing skill has one paragraph saying work items have no `stage` and progress belongs to a workflow run, and the rest of the skill routes by stage and a `workflowStep` field.

payload.blocks: Clusters 12 to 14 and 19 and conflict C7 of the rule gathering, which concern how agents ask the owner; and through them the start-context plan's AGENTS.md cut. Everything else of the gathering lands.
payload.headline: Rewrite the asking-a-person doctrine in the gathering, or wait for the communication-standard plan?

parts.cause: The gathering parks those five items so that the rest lands. The earlier recommendation was that the standard plan lands first so each text moves once; but that plan is a draft nobody is running, so waiting for it would hold the gathering open and the plan after it with no date.

options.cost: None beyond the five parked items, about 40 lines.
options.does: The gathering moves the doctrine now; the standard plan, still a draft, rebases on the moved unit when it is written.
options.gain: Nothing waits on a draft; each text moves once for the code that exists.
options.harm: The standard plan must start from the moved text.
options.label: A. Gathering first

options.cost: Unknown: depends on when the standard plan is run.
options.does: The five items stay parked until the standard plan is planned and done.
options.gain: Each text is written once, by the plan that owns the idea.
options.harm: Open-ended wait; the gathering and the start-context plan after it cannot finish.
options.label: B. Standard plan first

options.cost: About one extra day of work.
options.does: The first phase of the standard plan is done inside the gathering.
options.harm: A larger phase and a lost separate review.
options.label: C. Fold the standard into the gathering

parts.recommendation: A: it lets the chain finish and costs the draft plan nothing it has not yet written. This changes the earlier recommendation, which assumed the standard plan would run first.

scope.allows: Moving the doctrine on asking a person to one owner unit and settling conflict C7 as part of the gathering.
scope.forbids: Writing the communication standard itself, or touching the other parked-free rows.

parts.what: Two plans want to rewrite the same doctrine on how agents ask the owner: the rule gathering (moves it to one owner unit) and the draft communication-standard plan (261122-1950), which is only a draft and is not running.
